## Fix landed for review — Gerrit 1987 (commit fd1a2ddec1)

### The message, before and after (both observed, not read off source)

Drove the real `_no_repo_commits` fixture in a disposable worktree by having a test run
`git commit --allow-empty` against the checkout. Before:

```
Test moved the repo HEAD (cc3fba5cfb -> 018dbb1462): it committed into the rebar checkout
instead of an isolated tmp tracker. Isolate the git writes - pin GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES to
the tmp root (see tests/scripts/graph/conftest.py::_isolate_git_from_enclosing_repo) or init
the tracker as its own git repo. Undo the stray commit(s) with: git reset --hard cc3fba5cfb
```

After, from the same probe re-run against the fix:

```
The repo HEAD moved during this test (cc3fba5cfb -> ac939983b7). The guard only samples HEAD
around each test, so it cannot tell which process committed.
If this test committed, isolate its git writes - pin GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES to the tmp root
(see tests/scripts/graph/conftest.py::_isolate_git_from_enclosing_repo) or init the tracker
as its own git repo.
If it did not, a concurrent commit from outside the suite looks identical here: a detached run
shares this checkout with whatever else is committing, rebasing, or switching branches in it.
So do not run the recovery below until you know the moved HEAD is yours - it discards another
process's commit and every uncommitted change in this worktree.
Once you own the commit(s), undo them with: git reset --hard cc3fba5cfb
```

### What it conditions on

Nothing detectable - deliberately. Two `git rev-parse HEAD` samples carry no attribution signal,
exactly as `746c-185a-0e48-4b83` concluded for the leak guard's snapshot diff, so there is no
"did this process move HEAD" predicate to branch on. Rather than assert the common case, the
message states the limit outright ("the guard only samples HEAD around each test, so it cannot
tell which process committed"), names both causes, and gates the destructive step on the READER's
knowledge: the warning is placed BEFORE the command, because a caveat read after it is read too
late. The recovery is still offered verbatim - it is the right remedy for whoever owns the commit.

### Detection unchanged

`_no_repo_commits` still fails on any HEAD move, which is correct: the code under test changed and
later results are suspect regardless of who moved it. The fixture's body is a one-line swap of the
inline f-string for a call to the extracted `head_move_failure_message`; the `before`/`after`
sampling, the `allow_repo_writes` opt-out, and the `pytest.fail` are byte-identical. Proven twice:
the extraction was verified to emit the ORIGINAL text verbatim end-to-end before any wording
changed, and the new end-to-end self-test observes the real fixture raising on a real HEAD move.

### RED -> GREEN and mutation

Three tests, all confirmed RED before the fix existed and held out from the fix subagent (the
files were removed from its working tree and declared off-limits; it reported reading none):

- `tests/unit/test_external_mutation_diagnostics.py::test_head_move_message_does_not_prescribe_an_unconditional_reset`
  - RED: "no explicit do-not-reset warning".
- `tests/unit/test_external_mutation_diagnostics.py::test_head_move_message_does_not_assert_the_test_committed`
  - RED: "'committed into the rebar checkout instead of' is contained here".
- `tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py::test_head_move_guard_warns_before_it_offers_the_destructive_recovery`
  - drives the REAL fixture via a new `_drive_head_move_guard`, modelled on the `_drive_leak_guard`
    helper added by `746c-185a-0e48-4b83`; asserts on the message the guard actually raises, not on
    a private symbol or a source grep. RED against the old wording.

GREEN against the fix (21 passed across both files). Mutation check: re-seeded the exact confirmed
defect by restoring the original message body verbatim - all three returned RED (3 failed, 18
passed), including the end-to-end one, whose failure text shows the real guard emitting the old
message. Fix restored, 21 passed again.

Refactoring litmus: every assertion is on returned/raised message text, so a rename or extraction
that preserves the wording cannot turn them red.

### Scope and safety

- Caller sweep: the only two consumers of this text are `tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:290`
  (which matches against the self-test's own inline REPLICA conftest, not this message - unaffected)
  and `docs/local-dev-env.md:442`, which quotes the opening phrase and is updated in the same commit.
  Both incidental; no behavioural dependency.
- Restoration, not creation: no new entry point, no user-visible artifact, no mutating call.
- No new dependency; `head_move_failure_message` is pure and imports nothing.
- No test weakened: the only deleted line in any test file is an import, replaced by a combined one.
  No pre-existing assertion was touched, and none needed to be.

### Sibling sweep

Axis 1 (construct - "shared-checkout diagnostic asserting an unknowable cause"): the family has
three members. The leak guard was fixed under `746c-185a-0e48-4b83`; the HEAD-move guard is fixed
here; the third, `pytest_sessionfinish`'s working-tree backstop, still says "(a test wrote into the
working tree instead of tmp_path)" on the same unavailable evidence. It prescribes no destructive
remedy, so it is materially milder and outside this ticket's stated scope - filed as
`inner-honourable-bluejay` (938d-d6e9-2580-4faa), linked `discovered_from` this bug. A repo-wide
`reset --hard` grep found no other destructive remedy inside a test diagnostic.

Axis 2 (parity census): CLI / MCP / library-facade surfaces are N/A - these are pytest fixtures, not
rebar surfaces. Automated callers = the three guards above (two fixed, one filed). Dual-direction:
the replica conftest at `test_repo_isolation_guard.py:237` emits its own abbreviated string, but it
exists to exercise wiring and is never shown to a developer as guidance - N/A.

### Gates

`make lint` exit 0; `make typecheck` clean (615 files); complexity ratchet `active=49 new=0
increased=0 stale=0`. Full unit + interfaces sweep: 13900 passed, 53 skipped, 1 xfailed. That sweep
initially surfaced one repo-wide oracle failure that the fast gates do not run -
`test_comment_hygiene_guard::test_the_real_tree_is_clean` flagged a dated incident in one of my new
docstrings; corrected by citing this bug's alias instead of the bare date, and the guard now passes.

### Replication

Re-ran the original reproduction (a test committing into the checkout) through the real guard: it
still fails the run - `1 passed, 1 error`, the error raised at teardown from `tests/conftest.py` -
and the printed remedy is now fenced. The user-visible problem, a diagnostic that tells an innocent
reader to destroy someone else's work, no longer reproduces.
